related_questions.question: Where do people go when they have bad mental health?

text_blocks.snippet: When experiencing poor mental health, individuals can seek help from various sources depending on the severity and nature of their concerns. Primary care providers, mental health professionals like psychologists and psychiatrists, and community support services are common starting points. For immediate crises, crisis resolution and home treatment teams, or emergency services at a hospital, can provide urgent care.
snippet_highlighted_words: Primary care providers, mental health professionals like psychologists and psychiatrists, and community support services are common starting points

list.snippet: A general practitioner (GP) can conduct an initial mental health screening and refer you to a specialist.
They can also provide guidance and support for managing mild to moderate mental health conditions.
Psychologists: Provide therapy and counseling to address mental health issues.
Psychiatrists: Medical doctors specializing in mental health, who can diagnose and prescribe medication.
Clinical social workers: Provide therapy and support, often focusing on social and environmental factors affecting mental health.
Mental health counselors/therapists: Offer various types of therapy to address specific mental health concerns.

list.title: Community Mental Health Teams (CMHTs):
list.snippet: Provide a range of mental health services, often coordinating care for individuals with more complex needs.

list.title: Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Teams (CRHTs):
list.snippet: Offer urgent mental health support, including crisis intervention and home treatment.

list.title: Residential care services:
list.snippet: Provide structured living environments for individuals needing more intensive support.

list.title: Social care services:
list.snippet: Offer practical support and assistance with daily living for individuals with mental health challenges.

list.title: Emergency services at a hospital:
list.snippet: Go to the A&E department of a local hospital if you are in immediate crisis or feel like you might harm yourself or others.

list.title: Crisis hotline:
list.snippet: Organizations like Samaritans (116 123) offer confidential support and can provide immediate help.
SAMHSA (Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration): Offers resources and a helpline (1-800-662-HELP) to find mental health services.
NIMH (National Institute of Mental Health): Provides information on various mental health conditions and resources for finding help.
Mental Health America (MHA): Offers a directory of mental health organizations and services.
State and county health agencies: May have information on mental health resources in your area.
Your primary care provider: Can be a starting point for finding mental health services.
